title: SIU clears Toronto police officers in death of teen
article: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has not found any reasonable grounds to lay criminal charges against police officers involved in a fatal incident during the attempted arrest of a Toronto man in May 2010.
Eighteen-year-old Junior Manon died while attempting to evade police following a routine traffic stop in the city's north end.
After a lengthy probe in which five regular SIU investigators and two forensic investigators interviewed dozens of officers and witnesses, SIU director Ian Scott cleared all police officers.
The SIU is an arm's length agency that investigates incidents involving police resulting in death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault.

Mr. Manon was pulled over by police just after 6:30 p.m. on May 5 near the intersection of Steeles Avenue and Keele Street for a minor traffic violation. When the two officers checked their computer system, they found Mr. Manon was in breach of a probation condition prohibiting him from driving a car.

One officer arrested Mr. Manon and attempted to handcuff him, but the man broke free, darting across Steeles Avenue and onto Founders Road, on the York University grounds. Both officers pursued Mr. Mamon on foot, eventually taking Mr. Manon down on a grassy area on the east side of Founders Road, north of Ian McDonald Boulevard.
A struggled ensued during which time one of the officers put their weight on Mr. Manon's upper body in an effort to control him, Mr. Scott said in a statement issued Thursday.
"At one point, Mr. Manon attempted to get up as if he was doing a push up with his arms, but the weight from the officers prohibited him from doing so," he said.
Soon, nine other police officers arrived and Mr. Manon "went limp."
"Mr. Manon was unconscious and unresponsive, and was placed in a recovery position by being moved on to his left side with one of his knees placed near his waist," Mr. Scott said.

"One officer saw blood on Mr. Manon's mouth and noticed that his eyelids flickered. The officer checked for a pulse on the side of Mr. Manon's neck and found one that was strong at first and then became weaker. Another officer noted a pulse when he checked for one in his wrist area."
When paramedics arrived around 6:50 p.m., Mr. Manon had no vital signs. He was transported to Humber River Regional Hospital, but was pronounced dead a short time later.
The province's chief forensic pathologist concluded that the cause of death was "positional asphyxia" following struggle and exertion.

"During a struggle with the two subject officers after he fell or was taken to the ground, pressure was placed on his chest in a manner that could have caused it to compress and interfere with his breathing," Mr. Scott said.

"I am of the view that the force used to arrest him was not excessive in these circumstances. His demise by means of positional asphyxia following exertion and struggle was tragic, but the subject officers cannot be held criminally liable for this unintended consequence of what was probably a lawful apprehension."
